meta.title: The Minor You Already Own
meta.summary: Aeolian is the natural minor scale you already own in full, with no characteristic note of its own — its job in this chapter is to be the plain minor that Dorian and Phrygian each change by turning one dial.

Two of Them Are Already Yours
already handled the rename from natural minor to Aeolian — the two names point at the same seven notes.
It has no characteristic note. No chip lights amber on the card headed

, no dot gets outlined in its windows. That's by construction — a characteristic note is whatever separates a scale from its nearest plain relative, and Aeolian is the plain relative, the reference the rest of this chapter gets measured against.
Play it against the drone. One card, and nothing on it lights up — that absence is half the lesson, heard rather than read. There is nothing here to point at.

Aeolian is a hinge rather than a destination. It sits between Dorian and Phrygian on the brightness ladder, both of its dials at the reference setting, and its job in this chapter is to be the thing the other two are heard against — not a fact to apologise for, just a fact about what it's for.
